label: Worsening (pandemic reversal)
rationale: Global HALE at birth fell from its 2019 peak of 63.5 years to 61.9 years in 2021, a 1.6-year drop that erased roughly a decade of gains. No official data exists beyond 2021, so the recovery trajectory is unknown; national life-expectancy proxies show only partial recovery.

label: Distant
rationale: Current 10-year solid tumor survival is roughly 50–60% overall, and metastatic cases cluster at 8–35% five-year survival, far from the 80% target. 2025 brought new approvals and the MSK MMRd immunotherapy-only trial (~80% response), but the target needs transformational advances in late-stage treatment.

label: Approaching
rationale: Only ~14% of US and ~6% of UK cancers are detected through screening, with effective screening for just 4–5 cancer types. 2025 brought strong momentum: the first FDA-cleared Alzheimer's blood tests and PATHFINDER 2 showing a 7× cancer-detection increase, with MCED tests approaching FDA PMA (expected H1 2026); cardiovascular and metabolic pre-symptomatic detection still lag.

label: Distant
rationale: Dementia prevalence after age 80 is ~17–24%, 4–5× the 5% target. Anti-amyloid therapies slow but do not stop decline, and 2025 saw failures of oral semaglutide and the anti-tau antibody posdinemab plus fatal ARIA-E safety warnings for Leqembi.

label: Approaching (but not achieved)
rationale: Best demonstrated human biological age reversals cluster around 2–4 years, far short of the 10-year threshold. The OpenAI/Retro >50× reprogramming-efficiency result and partial reprogramming moving toward human trials are promising.

label: Distant: no measured pre-symptomatic share for any NCD class; tools cleared, >50% not in sight
rationale: The ledger has no measurement, and so no trend, of the milestone's own quantity: the share of major NCD cases caught before symptoms. The verified FDA-cleared Alzheimer's blood tests (Lumipulse, Elecsys pTau181) are for patients with cognitive symptoms, not for pre-symptomatic screening. The multi-cancer results (PATHFINDER 2, Cancerguard) are legacy proponent reports with no population-scale uptake, and there are no cardiovascular or metabolic records. With no evidenced path to >50% across the four disease classes, the ETA exceeds 10 years (red).

basis.rule: Milestone red: no evidenced path. There is no measured value or trend of the milestone's quantity (share of major NCDs caught pre-symptomatic); tool clearances and a trial whose results are only expected (projection) cannot lift a status; ETA >10 years
basis.eta: >10 years (not estimable: no series of the pre-symptomatic detection share in the ledger)
basis.path: None evidenced at population scale. Cancer: MCED tests (Galleri PATHFINDER 2: >7x detection when added to USPSTF screening, 53.5% early-stage; Cancerguard launched), both legacy proponent reports; NHS-Galleri RCT results only expected (projection). Neurodegeneration: FDA-cleared blood tests for symptomatic evaluation. Cardiovascular/metabolic: no evidence records
blockers: Evidential: no population-level measurement of pre-symptomatic detection for any of the four disease classes
Technical/regulatory: no MCED test has regulatory approval or a mortality-benefit RCT result in the ledger; the cleared AD blood tests are indicated for symptomatic patients
basis.benchmark: >50% of major NCD cases (cancer, cardiovascular, metabolic, neurodegeneration) caught pre-symptomatic

label: Distant: US 5-yr survival 69% all cancers, metastatic 8-31% vs goal 80% of solid tumors at 10 yrs
rationale: The latest level in the ledger is 69% 5-year survival for all US cancers and 8-31% for stage IV disease (ACS/SEER 2025, legacy); 10-year survival is necessarily lower, far from 80% of solid tumors surviving 10 years. The ledger has no survival time series to extrapolate. The verified 2025 FDA approvals (Datroway, avutometinib+defactinib, imlunestrant, Pluvicto expansion) are incremental per-indication gains, and the NCI budget faces a proposed 37% cut. No evidenced path reaches the goal within 10 years (red, Distant).

label: Distant: ~17-24% at 80+ vs <5% goal; incidence -20% over 2-3 decades, >100 yrs to goal
rationale: Dementia prevalence after 80 is about 24% at ages 80-89 (US ADAMS, legacy), and the NHS gives 1 in 6 over-80s for Alzheimer's alone, against a target below 5%. The only trend evidence is a ~20% fall in age-standardized incidence over 2-3 decades in high-income countries (Lancet Commission 2024, legacy), about 0.7-1.1%/yr relative; extrapolated, reaching 5% takes more than 100 years. Interventions help only at the margin: intensive BP control gave RR 0.85 (verified) and anti-amyloid drugs slow decline, while oral semaglutide failed Phase 3 (verified). The ETA is therefore well over 10 years (red, Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: ETA >10 years by trend extrapolation. A ~20% incidence decline per 2-3 decades (0.7-1.1%/yr relative) takes ln(17-24/5)/rate = ~110-210 years to reach <5%
basis.eta: >100 years on the evidenced incidence trend (110-210 years if prevalence tracks age-standardized incidence)
basis.path: Risk-factor reduction (cardiovascular health, education; intensive BP control RR 0.85) plus anti-amyloid drugs that slow decline (donanemab -27% progression risk at 3 yrs, legacy); no intervention prevents or reverses dementia at scale
blockers: Technical: disease-modifying therapies slow but do not stop decline; 2025 Phase 3 failures (oral semaglutide, posdinemab)
basis.benchmark: Dementia prevalence (CDR>=1) after age 80 < 5%
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays red, but its grounds are corrected. The previous label 'Distant' gave no level or benchmark. label: Stalled: best human clock reversal ~2.5-3.2 yrs (2019-2025) vs >=10 yrs; no disease-incidence data
rationale: The best human biological-age reversals in the ledger are 2.5 years (TRIIM 2019), 3.23 years (Fitzgerald 2021) and 2.6 years (Buck TPE+IVIG 2025), all legacy, so the 2025 result shows no gain on 2019-21. The larger 7.42-year figure is an in-vitro preprint (SB000), the OpenAI/Retro result measured reprogramming efficiency rather than organismal age, and human reprogramming trials are only planned or just dosed. With the milestone quantity stalled, the ETA exceeds 10 years (red).

label: Distant: US 5-yr survival 69%, stage IV 8-31% vs 80% at 10 yrs; ~1%/yr hazard gains, ETA ~2063
rationale: US 5-year relative survival for all cancers is 69% (ACS 2025) and stage IV 5-year survival is 8-31%. That implies ~62% 10-year survival against the 80% target, a 1.9x gap in the non-surviving fraction. Non-survival has historically fallen ~1.0-1.2%/yr. With modest acceleration (median 1.5%/yr) from ADCs, bispecifics, immunotherapy and early detection, plus the 10-year follow-up floor, the median ETA is ~2063 (80% range 2042 to after 2100). That is far beyond 10 years, so red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: median ETA 2063 > made_at + 10 yr (RUBRIC.md §4: Distant)

eta.method: trend (exponential hazard reduction of the 10-yr non-surviving fraction, US frontier proxy) + structural floor (10-yr follow-up), Monte Carlo; cross-checked against a reference class and the prev ETA
eta.calc: Gap: 10-yr survival ~62% (5-yr 69% x ~0.90 conditional 5->10; breast 10-yr 86%) vs 80% -> non-survival 38% -> 20% = 1.9x (0.93 halvings). Historical rate (ACS, background): 5-yr survival 49% (1975-77) -> 69% (2014-20) = ln(51/31)/41 = 1.21%/yr; 67% -> 69% (2008-14 -> 2014-20) = 1.04%/yr. Time = ln(1.9)/r: r 1.1% -> 58 yr -> cohort 2071, observed ~2078; r 1.5% -> 43 yr -> cohort 2056, observed ~2063; r 3% -> observed ~2041. MC (N=200k): r ~ lognormal(median 1.5%, p10 0.8%), S10 ~ U(0.58, 0.66) for 2013 cohorts, observation lag U(5, 9) yr -> p10 2042.4, p50 2062.5, P(by 2100) 0.90; the global reading is later -> p90 null. P(by Oct 2036) 0.03. AI driver (robots-software metr-50-horizon-by-release 0.05 -> 1044.78 min 2019-02 -> 2026-04, ~6-month doubling; 2025-01-01-ai-drugs-75-in-trials) shortens discovery but not trials or the 10-yr follow-up. Prev v1 ETA was '>10 years', a band.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: US cancer mortality decline accelerating to >3%/yr; NHS-Galleri/MCED mortality benefit and uptake; mRNA vaccine (mRNA-4157) OS benefit across tumour types; durable stage IV survival with ADC/bispecific regimens. Later: NCI cut enacted; flat 5-yr survival in the next ACS releases; screening lead-time artefacts. Gather: an all-site 10-yr relative survival series (SEER/CONCORD/CRUK).

Central path: 2030 24%, 2035 31%, 2040 43%, 2043 50.1%. MC (N=200k; common midpoint shift N(0, 6 yr), per-class N(0, 4 yr), ceilings +/-10 pts): p10 2037, p50 2044, p90 2052; p90 widened to 2060 for the stricter 'each class >50%' reading (~2049 central) and non-HIC populations. P(by Oct 2036) 0.09. Reference class (background): US mammography ~29% -> ~70% in ~13 yr after 1987; CRC screening ~35% -> ~70% in ~20 yr; lung LDCT ~16-18% after 9 yr. label: Advancing: first approved stem-cell neuron grafts and brain-crossing drug; no repair for dementia
rationale: In March 2026 Japan conditionally approved grafts made from reprogrammed stem cells that replace the dopamine neurons lost in Parkinson's disease, the first approved treatment that replaces lost neurons rather than slowing their loss, and the FDA approved the first large-molecule drug engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier, a route for getting such drugs into the whole brain; in September the FDA approved the first treatment for the rare Alexander disease, which cuts production of the protein that builds up in the brain. label: Advancing: DNA marks read by aging clocks shown to cause disease; nothing predicts what works
rationale: In June 2026 a study of a rare inherited syndrome, in patients and mice, gave experimental evidence on a question researchers had called key and unanswered: the build-up of chemical marks on DNA that 'epigenetic clocks' read to estimate biological age can cause aging-like disease of blood, bone and metabolism, not merely track age; other peer-reviewed work traced inflammation, immune-cell and gut-microbe changes to organ and memory decline in mice, and found that the obesity drug semaglutide lengthens the lives of old female mice. No model yet ties these processes together well enough to predict which intervention extends healthy life in people without tradeoffs: none of eleven regimens in the US government's mouse lifespan programme worked, and in a small trial in older adults the leading anti-aging candidate rapamycin blunted the gains from exercise. ARPA-H is funding the first trials meant to open a regulatory path for drugs that target aging itself.

label: Advancing: blood p-tau217 flags Alzheimer's years ahead; cancer blood test missed main trial goal
rationale: In July 2026 a study pooling six groups of about 2,700 cognitively healthy older adults confirmed across independent cohorts that a blood test flags Alzheimer's years before symptoms: those with very high blood levels of the protein p-tau217 had about a 38% chance of cognitive impairment within five years and 78% within ten; peer-reviewed blood-protein panels also predicted lung cancer more than five years ahead and dated the onset of inherited ALS to within about a year and a half. The flagship test of cancer screening by blood fell short: in the 142,000-person NHS-Galleri trial, three yearly rounds of testing rarely raised a false alarm (specificity about 99.5%) but did not reduce stage III–IV cancers, and the 14% fall in stage IV could be chance; most new signatures have still not been checked by following ordinary symptom-free people from the general population over time, and this year's cleared Alzheimer's blood tests are for people who already have symptoms. The FDA's decision on Galleri, the first multi-cancer blood test up for approval, is pending after its advisory panel voted 7–2 in favour in September.

rationale: In June 2026 the FDA approved the first therapy built from regulatory T cells, the immune system's own brakes, after a randomized trial in which it raised one-year survival free of chronic graft-versus-host disease (donor immune cells attacking the patient after a stem-cell transplant) from 38% to 78%, and China approved the first CAR-T therapy, immune cells engineered to hunt one target, for a solid tumour, stomach cancer; a personalised mRNA cancer vaccine met its main goal in a large melanoma trial, and one-off CAR-T 'immune resets' that clear out a patient's misfiring immune cells kept most people with severe lupus and related diseases off immune drugs. Kyverna expects to complete its US filing for a CAR-T in stiff person syndrome in late 2026.

Drugs that clear or lower harmful brain proteins keep failing to protect thinking: the GLP-1 drug semaglutide and an antibody against tau, a protein that clumps in Alzheimer's brains, failed to slow the disease, a Parkinson's drug failed, and Roche dropped a Huntington's drug that lowered its target protein without helping patients. Biogen plans a late-stage trial of its tau-lowering drug, and Arrowhead expects its first data in Alzheimer's patients for an injected tau-silencing drug in 2027.

label: Advancing: DNA marks read by aging clocks shown to cause disease; nothing predicts what works
rationale: In June 2026 a study of a rare inherited syndrome, in patients and mice, showed that the build-up of chemical marks on DNA that 'epigenetic clocks' read to estimate biological age can cause aging-like disease of blood, bone and metabolism, not merely track age; other peer-reviewed work traced inflammation, immune-cell and gut-microbe changes to organ and memory decline in mice. No model yet ties these processes together well enough to predict which treatment extends healthy life in people without tradeoffs: none of eleven regimens in the US government's mouse lifespan programme worked, and in a small trial in older adults rapamycin, the leading anti-aging candidate, did not improve the gains from exercise and may have reduced them. A government-funded late-stage trial of three repurposed drugs is meant to open a regulatory path for drugs that target aging itself.

label: Advancing: blood p-tau217 flags Alzheimer's years ahead; cancer blood test missed main trial goal
rationale: In July 2026 a study pooling six groups of about 2,700 cognitively healthy older adults confirmed that a blood test flags Alzheimer's years before symptoms: those with very high levels of the protein p-tau217 had about a 38% chance of cognitive impairment within five years and 78% within ten; peer-reviewed blood-protein panels also predicted lung cancer more than five years ahead and dated the onset of inherited ALS to within about a year and a half. The flagship trial of cancer screening by blood fell short: in the 142,000-person NHS-Galleri trial, yearly testing rarely raised a false alarm (about 99.5% specificity) but did not reduce stage III–IV cancers, and most new signatures have not yet been tested by following ordinary symptom-free people over time. The FDA's decision on Galleri, the first multi-cancer blood test up for approval, is pending after its advisory panel voted 7–2 in favour in September.

label: Advancing: first approved regulatory T-cell therapy; deaths paused some autoimmune CAR-T trials
rationale: In June 2026 the FDA approved the first therapy built from regulatory T cells, the immune system's own brakes, after a randomized trial in which it raised one-year survival free of chronic graft-versus-host disease (donor immune cells attacking the patient after a stem-cell transplant) from 38% to 78%; one-off 'immune resets' with engineered CAR-T cells kept most people with severe lupus and related diseases off immune drugs, and a ten-year follow-up found a single CAR-T infusion still holding lymphoma off in 32% to 47% of patients depending on the lymphoma type, though their ten-year risk of a second cancer was 21%. Making such reprogramming safe and lasting is the open problem: in August Novartis halted its autoimmune CAR-T trials after three patients died of an inflammatory syndrome and Bristol Myers Squibb paused enrolment in its own; about 12% of reset patients relapsed, typically about a year after treatment; and a type 1 diabetes tolerance vaccine and two mRNA cancer vaccines failed. Kyverna expects to complete its US filing for a CAR-T in stiff person syndrome in late 2026.

label: Inching: senolytics reduced liver scarring; lasting in-body rejuvenation remains unproven
rationale: In October 2026 a small double-blind trial found that the drug pair dasatinib plus quercetin, which clears worn-out 'senescent' cells, reduced liver scarring in 8 of 17 patients with fatty liver disease versus 1 of 14 on placebo, and Life Biosciences' trial of a gene therapy that partly reprograms eye cells inside the body reported no serious side effects in its first three glaucoma patients after two months. Neither yet shows that cells can be reset inside the human body safely and lastingly: the liver result is small and unrepeated, prolonged reprogramming kills mice through liver failure, and the best senolytic drugs leave some senescent cells alive. Life Biosciences is moving to a higher dose, and NewLimit plans to take a liver reprogramming therapy into human trials in 2027.
